slides.headline: A speculative story set in Mumbai just won one of the world's biggest short-story prizes.
Sharon Aruparayil won the Asia regional prize in the 2026 Commonwealth Short Story Prize
slides.body: Her story 'Mehendi Nights,' a speculative tale set in Mumbai and published by Granta, was named the Asia region's winning entry when regional results were announced in May 2026.

slides.headline: The prize draws entries from across the entire Commonwealth - more than 50 countries.
slides.body: Regional winners receive £2,500 each, with one of the five eventually named overall winner - Aruparayil's win put an Indian voice and an Indian setting at the center of one of the literary world's most internationally diverse competitions.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat needs its stories told on the same stage as the rest of the world's literature.
slides.body: A speculative story set in Mumbai beating out entries from across the Commonwealth shows Indian fiction competing - and winning - on purely literary terms, not as a regional curiosity.
